lens: design concept, art direction, hierarchy and restraint vs ref-02

measurements.left_edges_css: Every column has one left edge (60 / 264 / 468). The wordmark ink starts at 57, 3 px outside the text edge, which is acceptable optical overshoot for the C.
measurements.header_levels: H2 is DM Sans 600 12.5 px, tracked caps, #8F4F10, at x 60/60/264/468. H3 is Fraunces italic 15.5 px. The H3 rows line up across columns at y 764 and 920. There is one style per level.
measurements.column_bottoms: Spirits, Wine and Beer & Cider all end at y 996, which gives a bottom margin of 60 and matches the top (60).
measurements.margins: The left, top and bottom margins are 60 css (15.9 mm). The art bleeds on the right. The Beer & Cider text ends at x ~648, leaving 168 css (44.5 mm) of empty paper to the right edge in the lower third. The column is declared as 288 wide, but the text uses about 180 of it.
measurements.price_pair_eye_travel: Every price sits inline about 1 em after its name. The worst row is Brown Butter Old Fashioned: about 18 px hop, roughly 5% of the 384 measure. No row is over 40%.
measurements.vertical_rhythm: Cocktails: Margarita block end to Manhattan is about 32 px, and Manhattan end to the House Originals head is about 40 px. The Cocktails end (662) to the Spirits/Wine heads (732) is a 70 px gap. The Beer head starts at 674, 58 px higher than Spirits and Wine, so the lower tier does not share a top line.
measurements.contrast_worst_pixel: Section heads are 5.48:1 and descriptions, prices and sub heads 6.6:1 (contrast.json). I checked CANTINA's glyph area myself: over the band y 41-115.5, navy (29,31,63) against paper (244,237,225) gives 13.67:1, which matches the proposal's 13.7:1. contrast.json's 1.0:1 comes only from the beam inside its box.
measurements.accent_area: 0.32% of the page and 0.11% of the text area. Only one region is dominant (20.48%).
measurements.bleed: The art extends 12 css (3.2 mm) past trim, and all text sits inside the 60 css inset.
measurements.device_count: 13 devices after subtraction, 3 of 16 removed (19%). That is below the 25% subtraction target in scorecard 1c.
measurements.phone: I checked the phone version from geometry only (preview not opened within the tool budget). It stacks Cocktails, Spirits, Wine, Beer & Cider in a frame at x 24-366.

remove: The 3-px amber misregistration trap. It is the dark sliver on the ground line at x 468-538 under the navy column, and in print it reads as a rendering error, not as print character.
top_problem: The big idea (an Iowa grain elevator pierced as papel picado, with CANTINA standing on its gallery) is ownable and passes the substitution test only on paper. The render doesn't carry it through. The elevator reads as a white block with pale stripes (a colonnade, a bank, a factory sawtooth), and the Mexican half rests on three 9-px diamonds that disappear at thumbnail size. Beside ref-02's painterly agave and floral boards, this flat vector art has no craft, no material surface and no warmth. It is a clean corporate diagram, not a cantina.
fixes: Make the picado read at thumbnail. Cut one large, recognisable papel picado motif through the bin walls (bigger rombos with the drilled circle-and-diamond pattern at 3-4x the current scale, amber showing through), so the Mexican half of the fusion is seen, not just explained in proposal.md.

Restore the reading order and the shared top line. Start Beer & Cider at y 732 with Spirits and Wine, and give the reclaimed 58 px to the elevator's base. Then fill or remove the 168-css empty field right of the Beer text, either by widening the column's content use or by bringing the art's right tier down beside it.
Take out the Cocktails padding. Set one item gap and one group gap (the +8 px stretch shows), and make Cocktails-to-lower-tier one deliberate interval, not a 70 px leftover.

Give the art a materiality that matches its two-ink print claim. Use flat ink with real density variation and a crisp cut-paper edge or shadow on the elevator, kept away from the reading zone, so it can stand beside ref-02's textured boards instead of reading as a UI illustration.

Reconsider the navy strip between the text column and the headhouse (x 468-538). It works like a heavy frame leg with no job. Narrow it, or let the dusk field show a sliver of amber horizon there, so the L-shaped navy mass stops reading as a border.

lens: Items and prices against the draft, how complete the ingredient descriptions are, and section flow
top_problem: The content is honest but thin, and the flow sells this venue short. All 14 items and all 14 prices match draft_doc.json exactly (Manhattan 15, Margarita 15, Daiquiri 14, Brown Butter OF 16, Pilsner 7, IPA 8, Amber 7, Malbec 12, Pinot Grigio 11, Brut Rosé 13, Blanco 12, Añejo 16, Cognac 18, Dry Cider 8). Nothing is invented. The Manhattan correctly hides its aromatic bitters (public_components), and the only tasting note is the Margarita's, which the draft supplies. But 10 of the 14 descriptions only restate the item name or a category: 'Blanco tequila pour', 'VSOP Cognac pour', 'Dry red wine', 'Crisp pale lager'. Beer is the most-ordered category in a Mexican restaurant, yet it is pushed to a side column that the hierarchy cannot place in order. Its head sits at y 674, above Spirits and Wine at y 732, so on the letter page the reading order between Beer & Cider and Spirits/Wine is unclear. On the phone, beer comes last. The generic content is mostly the known data gap: Rob still has to supply beer ABV, wine grape/region and spirit brand/age, and that is not the designer's fault. The flow and the wrap treatment are the designer's.
problems: Data gap (not the designer's fault; waiting on Rob): beer and cider have no ABV, producer or style detail beyond the draft; Malbec and Pinot Grigio have no region or producer; Brut Rosé has no grape or region; the tequilas and the Cognac have no brand, age statement or pour size. proposal.md flags this correctly. As a result 10 of 14 descriptions only repeat the name or a class, which caps criterion 8 whoever is at fault.

Flow: the draft order is Cocktails, Beer, Wine, Spirits, Cider, and the scorecard suggests cocktails, beer, wine, spirits, NA. The design reorders this to Cocktails, Spirits, Wine, Beer & Cider and justifies it as 'agave-forward', but two neat tequila pours do not make a spirits program worth leading with. Meanwhile beer, a core category for a Mexican cantina, is last on the phone and on the letter page sits in an art-anchored column whose head is 58 px higher than Spirits/Wine. The reader cannot tell whether to read it second or last.

The Beer and Cider draft sections are merged into one head, 'Beer & Cider', with Cider demoted to a subhead. That is acceptable editorially, but proposal.md never states it as a structural change to the draft. The Margarita/Manhattan swap is disclosed.

Wrapped description lines begin with a leading separator ('· orange liqueur · agave syrup · lime wheel', '· house demerara syrup · lime coin', '· demerara syrup · aromatic bitters · orange peel'). At the left margin the leading middot reads like a bullet or a stray mark, not a continuation. Three of the four cocktails have one.

The cocktail garnishes (lime wheel, lime coin, orange peel, cocktail cherry) are cited to recipe_versions rows, not to the draft components. They are plausible and sourced by the proposal, but the Accuracy reviewer must confirm them against phg.recipe_versions.garnish. I did not treat them as invented.

Brown Butter Old Fashioned has public_visibility.house_recipe = false. The printed 'Brown butter-washed bourbon · demerara syrup · aromatic bitters · orange peel' matches the draft description's own disclosure, so it passes, but confirm with Rob that the itemised house-prep line is allowed on public copy.

Price format: inline, no $, whole numbers, tabular, muted, 0.75em after the name. This is consistent and the association is unambiguous, but the prices do not align from row to row and the muted #5B5058 makes them the weakest text on the page, so the guest has to hunt for them. The price treatment is safe, not crafted.

Cocktails rhythm: the gaps were inflated (+8 px per item and per group) to fill the page, so the Margarita-to-Manhattan and Classics-to-House Originals gaps feel loose and padded against the tight lower tier. The page looks like two different densities.

There is no non-alcoholic section. None is in the draft, so this is not a content_integrity failure, but a Mexican restaurant menu without aguas frescas, Jarritos or a zero-proof option is incomplete. Flag it to Rob.
fixes: Put Beer & Cider second in the reading path on both formats: on phone stack it Cocktails, Beer & Cider, Wine, Spirits; on letter make the column-3 head clearly read after Cocktails (for example align all three lower heads on one row) so the order is not ambiguous.
Remove the leading middot from continuation lines: break after a full ingredient with no separator, or set descriptions as comma-separated prose, so no line starts with a bullet-like mark.
Raise the price weight or colour to ink #221C22 (keep the lighter weight), so the price reads as the item's partner rather than a footnote, keeping the inline style.
Add a one-line note to proposal.md that the draft's Beer and Cider sections are merged under 'Beer & Cider', and ask Rob whether a non-alcoholic section should exist.

When Rob supplies the data, replace the name-echo descriptions with the formula: beer 'style · ABV · producer', wine 'grape · region', spirits 'brand · age/type · pour'. Until then keep the current draft text; do not invent anything.

lens: Ingredient/garnish/label trace to build/draft_doc.json and phg.recipe_versions; how descriptions and prices sit together in preview-letter.png; price-to-item gate. Verified: all 14 printed names and prices match draft_doc.json and phg.menu_items. Garnishes are right: Margarita 'lime wheel' (rv f06abb74), Manhattan 'cocktail cherry' (rv 9fb77eaa), House Daiquiri 'lime coin' (rv 14d45e57), Brown Butter OF 'orange peel' (rv 7095fd3d). Every cocktail ingredient traces to a draft component. The Manhattan's bitters are correctly hidden (public_components aromatic-bitters:false). 'house demerara syrup' and 'Bright and citrus-forward.' come from the draft desc. Spirits, wine, beer and cider lines are the draft/menu_items menu_description text word for word. The masthead '& cocktail bar · Iowa City, Iowa' is venue data. There are no taglines or captions that state item facts. No glassware or method is printed. Note for the Coordinator: phg.menu_items for project ddc4bb5b also has 'Junmai Ginjo' at 12 ('Junmai Ginjo sake.'). It is absent from draft_doc.json and from the menu, so the draft and the database disagree and the Content reviewer should settle it. It is not an invented fact. The recipe_components join came back empty (comps null for all four recipes), so ingredients were verified against the draft components.
top_problem: The facts are clean but the copy is thin. 8 of 14 descriptions are database classes, and 3 simply repeat the item name: 'Blanco Tequila' / 'Blanco tequila pour', 'Añejo Tequila' / 'Añejo tequila pour', 'Cognac VSOP' / 'VSOP Cognac pour'. 'Dry red wine', 'Dry white wine' and 'Crisp pale lager' read like taxonomy, not guest language. Only the Margarita gets a tasting note, so there are two voices. For a Mexican cantina in Iowa City, the Mexican identity lives only in the art and the word CANTINA. Headings are all English, there are only two agave pours, and the order puts Cocktails first with Spirits/Agave down in the lower tier next to Wine. Criterion 12 falls in the scorecard's automatic-fail band (<=40) and criterion 13 reads 'any bar with a papel-picado border'.
fixes: Replace the name-echo spirit lines with sourced guest language. Cite public.spirit_lexicon / public.beverage_categories rows for blanco (unaged) and añejo (aged) tequila and for the VSOP age class, or print no description line until Rob supplies brand and pour size. Never print a line that restates the name.

Give the wine, beer and cider lines one appetising voice built only from their draft words (for example 'Crisp, pale and dry' style phrasing that keeps 'crisp pale lager' / 'toasty amber lager'). Also decide the tasting-note rule: either every cocktail gets a sourced one-line note or none does, so the Margarita's italic line stops being a one-off.

Venue fit: add correct Spanish kickers to the section heads (for example 'Cócteles', 'Agave y Destilados', 'Vino', 'Cerveza y Sidra', with accents exactly as written) under the English heads. Ask the designer (as a layout note) to give Spirits/Agave more weight than Wine, since agave is this venue's signature category.

Layout note for the designer: continuation lines that begin with '· ' (Margarita, Daiquiri, Old Fashioned) read as bullets and look orphaned. Break before the separator and drop it, or break after it and hang it. Also balance the Margarita's first line: it wraps early (about 360 of 384 px) and leaves a 3-line stack. The inline price floats at a different x on every row (Brown Butter OF 16 sits about 190 px right of Manhattan 15). That is fine for association, but a tabular hanging position per column would read calmer.

Brown Butter Old Fashioned has public_visibility.house_recipe:false in draft_doc.json, yet it prints its full component list. Confirm with Rob that listing names without quantities is allowed. If it is not, cut the line to 'Brown butter-washed bourbon · orange peel' (component + rv 7095fd3d garnish).
